# Meets

> Local-first AI meeting transcription for macOS.

Meets is a free, open-source macOS application — a meetings-only fork of Muesli — that records meetings (mic + system audio) and transcribes them with on-device AI inference. All speech-to-text runs locally on Apple Silicon — no cloud required for core functionality.

## Features

- **Meeting Recording**: Records mic + system audio, merges them into a timestamped transcript
- **Live Meeting Transcripts**: Optional low-latency live captions during the meeting
- **Meeting Notes**: Optional AI-generated structured summaries (ChatGPT subscription, or BYOK OpenAI/OpenRouter, or local Ollama / LM Studio / custom LLM)
- **Speaker Diarization**: Identifies individual speakers in system audio
- **Meeting Insights**: Local analytics over your meeting history
- **Local-First**: Transcription runs entirely on-device via Fluid Audio / CoreML
- **Privacy**: Audio never leaves your Mac unless you opt into cloud summarization; iCloud sync transfers text and sync metadata, not audio
- **Free & Open Source**: MIT licensed, no subscriptions, no usage limits

## Technical Details

- **Runtime**: Native Swift/AppKit application (not Electron)
- **Speech Engine**: Fluid Audio SDK (CoreML, Apple Neural Engine)
- **Storage**: Local SQLite database at ~/Library/Application Support/Meets/
- **Audio Capture**: Microphone (You) + system audio (Others) via CoreAudio process tap
- **Platform**: macOS 14.2+ on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4)

## Architecture

Meets is a menu bar app whose core mode is meeting transcription:

1. **Start Recording**: User starts recording from the menu bar or the meeting hotkey → mic captures "You" audio, system audio captures "Others".
2. **Transcription**: Audio is transcribed locally with VAD-driven chunk rotation; diarization labels remote speakers; segments are merged by timestamp.
3. **Notes**: Optional LLM summarization produces structured notes (ChatGPT subscription or BYOK providers).
4. **Storage**: Transcripts, notes, and recordings are stored in local SQLite.

The app uses Fluid Audio's CoreML models running on the Apple Neural Engine for speech-to-text, minimizing CPU/GPU usage. Optional cloud integration is available for meeting note summarization and transcript cleanup, using bring-your-own-key configuration or a ChatGPT subscription.
